## Decision Context

- Decision to make: Which of four directions should the framework take to shorten the implementation phase, given the operator's criteria, and is building concurrent implementer work justified at all.
- Delivery constraints: Gates, validators, artifact contracts and one owner per phase hold as written; the runtime calls no model; the baseline is the 1h55m30s (6930 seconds) implementation phase of run-ded114f50a46 with suite time excluded from both sides; token cost may not exceed baseline by more than 25 percent unless the elapsed-time gain exceeds 40 percent; no decision deadline is stated (investigation report E-002, E-039). This is option analysis only: the committed recommendation is the next phase's output, and no command was run for this artifact.
- Assumptions in force: The token baseline is only a read estimate of 57746 tokens per dispatch, not measured usage (E-039, E-041; `Q-001`). The in-phase ceiling reads six tasks over a longest chain of four, about one third elapsed-time reduction, and treats task durations as equal because only complexity labels exist (E-029, E-030, E-031; `Q-003`). repositoryWrites.scope: none. This agent writes its own artifact and its result envelope, and nothing else. Product documentation living in the repository is proposed as content inside the artifact and applied by the role that owns the file, so a documentation change never travels as an unreviewed write.
repositoryWrites.rationale: This agent's authority is over what is said about a change, never over the change itself. Writing to the repository would let a publication step alter the delivered behavior it exists to describe, and the resulting document would then be accurate about a system this agent had just modified.

commandExecution.purpose: none. Every fact this agent publishes comes from a supplied artifact, and a fact obtained by running a command would be this agent producing evidence rather than communicating it.
prohibitedPurposes: any command that modifies production source or committed run evidence

determinism.contract: Identical inputs and an identical context snapshot must produce the same published statements, the same known-issue set, the same compatibility statement, the same declared release verdict, and the same declared artifact status.
determinism.orderingRule: Known issues keep the order of the source that recorded them, so a supplied defect list and the issues published from it can be read side by side.
determinism.modelIndependence: No module may reference a specific model, vendor, or agent runtime. Technology names are permitted only when they trace to the supplied evidence, release context, or repository context.

model_tier.basis: declared light for investigate/publication in config/model-tier-policy.json
